sw.B: Kisha Hezekia akamwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}},
sw.R: Kisha Hezekia akamwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Akasema,

decisions.choice: he prayed: the prayer of verses 16-20
decisions.reason: The parallel 2 Kings 19:15 reads "prayed before the LORD". The prayer praises God, asks him to listen, states the danger, and asks for rescue so that the world may know him.

source.text: יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אַתָּה־ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh of hosts, God of Israel, sitting [on] the cherubim, you he [is] the God, you alone, of all [the] kingdoms of the earth; you made the heavens and the earth.

en.L: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, God of Israel, who sits [on] the cherubim, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, the God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made the heavens and the earth.
en.B: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and no one else, are God of every kingdom on earth. It was {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who made the heavens and the earth.
en.R: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sit as king above the cherubim, the winged creatures over the ark of the covenant. Over all the kingdoms of the earth, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone are God. You made the heavens and the earth.

es.L: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, Dios de Israel, que estás sentado [sobre] los querubines, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} [eres] el Dios, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} solo, de todos los reinos de la tierra; {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} hiciste los cielos y la tierra.
es.B: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, Dios de Israel, que reinas entronizado sobre los querubines: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, y nadie más, eres Dios de todos los reinos de la tierra. Tú hiciste los cielos y la tierra.
es.R: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, Dios de Israel, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} reinas sentado sobre los querubines, los seres con alas que están sobre el arca del pacto. Solo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres Dios sobre todos los reinos de la tierra. Tú hiciste los cielos y la tierra.

sw.L: "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, uketiye [juu ya] makerubi, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} peke yako, wa falme zote za dunia; {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe uliyezifanya mbingu na dunia.
sw.B: "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, uliyeketi juu ya makerubi: {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, wala si mwingine, ndiwe Mungu wa kila ufalme duniani. Ni {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyezifanya mbingu na dunia.
sw.R: "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umeketi kama mfalme juu ya makerubi, viumbe wenye mabawa walio juu ya sanduku la agano. Wewe peke yako ndiwe Mungu juu ya falme zote za dunia. Wewe ndiwe uliyezifanya mbingu na dunia.

decisions.choice: who sits on the cherubim: enthroned above the winged figures over the ark
decisions.reason: Two golden cherubim spread their wings over the ark in the most holy place, and God was pictured as seated above them as king (Exodus 25:18-22; 1 Samuel 4:4; Psalm 99:1). The verb can mean to sit or to be enthroned.

decisions.choice: you alone are God: the LORD is the only God and the Maker of all things
decisions.reason: Against Sennacherib's claim that no god could resist him (verses 10-13), Hezekiah confesses that the LORD alone is God over every kingdom, because he made heaven and earth (44:24; 45:5-7). The parallel 2 Kings 19:15 lacks "of hosts".

decisions.choice: the winged creatures over the ark of the covenant
decisions.reason: Readable explains the cherubim.

decisions.choice: "BWANA wa majeshi"
decisions.reason: Isaiah's prayer opens with "the LORD of hosts" where 2 Kings has "the LORD"; otherwise the 2 Kings wording is kept.

source.text: הַטֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה׀אָזְנְךָ֙ וּֽשְׁמָ֔ע פְּקַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה עֵינֶ֖ךָ וּרְאֵ֑ה וּשְׁמַ֗ע אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י סַנְחֵרִ֔יב אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֔ח לְחָרֵ֖ף אֱלֹהִ֥ים חָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Incline, Yahweh, your ear and hear; open, Yahweh, your eyes and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib that he has sent to taunt [the] God living.

en.L: Incline, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear and hear; open, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to taunt the living God.
en.B: Turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and listen; open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and look. Hear every word Sennacherib has sent to insult the living God.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please listen and hear. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes and see. Listen to everything Sennacherib has said. He sent his message to insult the living God.

es.L: Inclina, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} oído y oye; abre, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos y mira; y oye todas las palabras de Senaquerib, que ha enviado para afrentar al Dios vivo.
es.B: Inclina {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} oído, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y escucha; abre {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y mira. Escucha todas las palabras que Senaquerib ha enviado para insultar al Dios vivo.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, por favor, escucha y oye. {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, abre {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos y mira. Escucha todo lo que ha dicho Senaquerib. Envió su mensaje para insultar al Dios vivo.

sw.L: Tega, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, sikio {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}, usikie; fumbua, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, uone; uyasikie maneno yote ya Senakeribu, aliyoyatuma kumtukana Mungu aliye hai.
sw.B: Tega sikio {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, usikie; fumbua macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uone. Sikia kila neno ambalo Senakeribu ametuma kumtukana Mungu aliye hai.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali sikiliza na usikie. Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, fumbua macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} uone. Sikiliza yote aliyosema Senakeribu. Alituma ujumbe wake ili kumtukana Mungu aliye hai.

decisions.choice: incline your ear, open your eyes: asking God to take notice and act
decisions.reason: The same plea appears in Daniel 9:18. It does not suggest God is deaf, but asks him to treat the matter as his own.

decisions.choice: which he has sent: Sennacherib sent the words through his messengers and his letter
decisions.reason: The words are those of the letter (verses 10-13) and of the Rabshakeh (36:4-20). They were sent to taunt the living God (verse 4).

decisions.choice: "maneno yote ... aliyoyatuma"
decisions.reason: Isaiah has "all the words ... which he has sent", so Sennacherib sends words, not a messenger; the relative changes to agree with "maneno".

source.text: אָמְנָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה הֶחֱרִ֜יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת־כָּל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת וְאֶת־אַרְצָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Truly, Yahweh, have laid waste the kings of Assyria all the lands and their land,

en.L: Truly, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the lands and their land,
en.B: It is true, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these lands and their territory,
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, it is true that the kings of Assyria have destroyed all these countries and their lands.

es.L: Es verdad, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que los reyes de Asiria han asolado todas las tierras y su tierra,
es.B: Es cierto, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que los reyes de Asiria han devastado todas estas tierras y sus territorios,
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, es verdad que los reyes de Asiria han destruido todos estos países y sus tierras.

sw.L: Kweli, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wafalme wa Ashuru wameziharibu nchi zote na nchi yao,
sw.B: Ni kweli, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwamba wafalme wa Ashuru wameziangamiza nchi hizi zote na maeneo yao,
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ni kweli kwamba wafalme wa Ashuru wameziangamiza nchi hizi zote na ardhi zao.

decisions.choice: all the lands and their land: the countries and the territory belonging to them
alternatives: the nations and their land (2 Kings 19:17)
decisions.reason: The phrase is awkward. The parallel 2 Kings 19:17 reads "the nations and their land". Both describe the same devastation, and the sense is not in doubt.

decisions.choice: truly: Hezekiah admits what Sennacherib said is true
decisions.reason: The facts are not in dispute (verses 11-13). The question is what they prove, which the next verse answers.

source.text: וְנָתֹ֥ן אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם בָּאֵ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֣י אִם־מַעֲשֵׂ֧ה יְדֵֽי־אָדָ֛ם עֵ֥ץ וָאֶ֖בֶן וַֽיְאַבְּדֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: and putting their gods in the fire, for not gods [were] they, but [the] work of [the] hands of humankind, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.

en.L: and have put their gods into the fire, for they [were] not gods, but the work of human hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
en.B: and have flung their gods into the fire. Those were never gods, only wood and stone shaped by human hands, so they could destroy them.
en.R: They threw the gods of those nations into the fire and burned them up. But those were not real gods. People had made them out of wood and stone. That is why the Assyrians could destroy them.

es.L: y han echado sus dioses al fuego, porque no [eran] dioses, sino obra de manos humanas, madera y piedra, y por eso los destruyeron.
es.B: y han arrojado sus dioses al fuego. Esos nunca fueron dioses, sino solo madera y piedra labradas por manos humanas; por eso pudieron destruirlos.
es.R: Echaron al fuego los dioses de esas naciones y los quemaron. Pero no eran dioses de verdad. La gente los había hecho de madera y de piedra. Por eso los asirios pudieron destruirlos.

sw.L: na kuitupa miungu yao motoni, kwa maana haikuwa miungu, bali kazi ya mikono ya wanadamu, miti na mawe; kwa hiyo wakaiangamiza.
sw.B: na kuitupa miungu yao motoni. Hiyo haikuwa miungu kamwe, ila miti na mawe yaliyochongwa kwa mikono ya wanadamu, kwa hiyo waliweza kuiangamiza.
sw.R: Waliitupa miungu ya mataifa hayo motoni, ikateketea. Lakini hiyo haikuwa miungu ya kweli. Watu walikuwa wameitengeneza kwa miti na mawe. Ndiyo sababu Waashuru waliweza kuiangamiza.

decisions.choice: not gods, but the work of human hands: idols have no power of their own
decisions.reason: Isaiah mocks idols as things made by craftsmen (2:8; 40:19-20; 44:9-20). Their defeat proves nothing about the LORD, who made the heavens and the earth (verse 16).

decisions.choice: putting: an infinitive continuing the verb of verse 18
decisions.reason: The form carries on the past action of the previous verse; 2 Kings 19:18 has the finite verb "they have put".

decisions.choice: burned them up; That is why the Assyrians could destroy them
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject and spells out that the gods could be destroyed because they were only objects.

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ מִיָד֑וֹוְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, Yahweh our God, save us from his hand, and may know all [the] kingdoms of the earth that you [are] Yahweh, you alone.

en.L: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone."
en.B: So now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, rescue us from his power, so that every kingdom on earth will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, save us from the king of Assyria. Then all the kingdoms of the earth will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

es.L: Ahora pues, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios nuestro, sálvanos de su mano, para que todos los reinos de la tierra sepan que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} [eres] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} solo».
es.B: Así que ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios nuestro, líbranos de su poder, para que todos los reinos de la tierra sepan que solo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.R: Ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios nuestro, sálvanos del rey de Asiria. Así todos los reinos de la tierra sabrán que solo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».

sw.L: Basi sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, utuokoe kutoka mkononi mwake, ili falme zote za dunia zijue ya kuwa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} [ndiwe] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} peke yako."
sw.B: Basi sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, utuokoe kutoka katika nguvu zake, ili kila ufalme duniani ujue kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} peke yako ndiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, utuokoe kutoka kwa mfalme wa Ashuru. Ndipo falme zote za dunia zitajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} peke yako ndiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

decisions.choice: that all may know that you alone are the LORD: the goal of the rescue is that the nations know God
decisions.reason: Hezekiah asks not only for safety but for God's name to be known (compare 45:6; 1 Kings 18:37). The parallel 2 Kings 19:19 reads "that you, LORD, are God alone".

decisions.choice: from his hand: from his power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control; "his" is Sennacherib.

decisions.choice: from the king of Assyria
decisions.reason: Readable names the one meant by "his".

decisions.choice: que tú eres el SEÑOR, tú solo
alternatives: que tú, SEÑOR, eres el único Dios
decisions.reason: Isaiah's Hebrew ends "that you are Yahweh, you alone", where 2 Kings 19:19 has "that you, Yahweh, are God alone"; the Spanish of Kings is changed to follow it.

decisions.choice: "wewe ndiwe BWANA, wewe peke yako"
alternatives: "wewe, Ee BWANA, ndiwe Mungu peke yako" (2 Kings 19:19)
decisions.reason: Isaiah ends "that you are the LORD, you alone", where 2 Kings has "that you, LORD, are God alone"; the Swahili follows Isaiah, and the vocative "Ee" falls away because the name is now the predicate.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ הִתְפַּלַּ֣לְתָּ אֵלַ֔י אֶל־סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Isaiah son of Amoz to Hezekiah, saying, Thus says Yahweh God of Israel: that you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,

en.L: And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Because you have prayed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,
en.B: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Because you have prayed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
en.R: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah. He said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: You prayed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about King Sennacherib of Assyria.

es.L: Entonces Isaías hijo de Amoz envió a decir a Ezequías: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel: Por cuanto {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has pedido en oración acerca de Senaquerib, rey de Asiria,
es.B: Entonces Isaías hijo de Amoz le mandó decir a Ezequías: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, dice esto: Puesto que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has hecho oración acerca de Senaquerib, rey de Asiria,
es.R: Entonces Isaías hijo de Amoz le envió un mensaje a Ezequías. Le dijo: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel: Tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pediste en oración acerca del rey Senaquerib de Asiria.

sw.L: Naye Isaya mwana wa Amozi akatuma kwa Hezekia, akisema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: Kwa kuwa umeniomba kuhusu Senakeribu mfalme wa Ashuru,
sw.B: Kisha Isaya mwana wa Amozi akatuma ujumbe kwa Hezekia: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: Kwa kuwa umeniomba kuhusu Senakeribu mfalme wa Ashuru,
sw.R: Kisha Isaya mwana wa Amozi alimtumia Hezekia ujumbe. Alisema, "Hiki ndicho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, anachosema: Uliniomba kuhusu mfalme Senakeribu wa Ashuru.

decisions.choice: because you have prayed: the prayer is the occasion of the answer
alternatives: as for what you have prayed
decisions.reason: The clause leads into verse 22. The parallel 2 Kings 19:20 adds "I have heard"; here the answer itself shows that the prayer was heard.

decisions.choice: he sent: Isaiah answers by a message, not in person
decisions.reason: Hezekiah prayed in the temple (verse 14); the answer comes through the prophet, as in verses 5-7. The message runs to verse 35, with a poem against Sennacherib in verses 22-29.

decisions.choice: "Kwa kuwa umeniomba ..."
decisions.reason: Isaiah has "because you have prayed" and no "I have heard", so the sentence runs on into verse 22; the published formula "BWANA ... asema hivi" is kept.

source.text: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן אַחֲרֶ֨יךָ֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הֵנִ֔יעָה בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: this [is] the word that has spoken Yahweh against him: she despises you, she mocks you, [the] virgin daughter of Zion; behind you a head she shakes, [the] daughter of Jerusalem.

en.L: this [is] the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against him: \q She despises you, she mocks you, the virgin daughter of Zion; \q behind you she shakes [her] head, the daughter of Jerusalem.
en.B: this is the word {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against him: \q The virgin, Daughter Zion, looks down on you and laughs at you; \q Daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at your back.
en.R: So this is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against him: \q The people of Zion are like a young woman no one has ever conquered. \q They look down on you and laugh at you. \q The people of Jerusalem shake their heads at you as you run away.

es.L: esta [es] la palabra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado contra él: \q Te desprecia, se burla de ti la virgen hija de Sion; \q detrás de ti menea la cabeza la hija de Jerusalén.
es.B: esta es la palabra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho contra él: \q La virgen, la hija Sion, te desprecia y se ríe de ti; \q la hija Jerusalén menea la cabeza a tus espaldas.
es.R: Por eso, este es el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho contra él: \q La gente de Sion es como una joven que nadie ha conquistado jamás. \q Te miran con desprecio y se ríen de ti. \q La gente de Jerusalén menea la cabeza mientras tú huyes.

sw.L: hili [ndilo] neno ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amelinena juu yake: \q Anakudharau, anakudhihaki, binti bikira wa Sayuni; \q nyuma yako anatikisa kichwa [chake], binti wa Yerusalemu.
sw.B: hili ndilo neno ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amelinena juu yake: \q Bikira, Binti Sayuni, anakudharau na kukucheka; \q Binti Yerusalemu anatikisa kichwa chake nyuma yako.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo huu ndio ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema juu yake: \q Watu wa Sayuni ni kama msichana ambaye hakuna adui aliyewahi kumshinda. \q Wanakudharau na kukucheka. \q Watu wa Yerusalemu wanakutikisia vichwa unapokimbia.

decisions.choice: the virgin daughter of Zion: Jerusalem pictured as a young woman no enemy has taken
decisions.reason: "Daughter Zion" pictures the city and its people as a young woman (1:8). "Virgin" adds that the invader has not violated her (compare 23:12).

decisions.choice: shakes her head behind you: mockery of an enemy who turns back
decisions.reason: Shaking the head was a gesture of scorn (Psalm 22:8; Lamentations 2:15). "Behind you" pictures Sennacherib retreating while the city mocks him.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion are like a young woman no one has ever conquered; as you run away
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the city and what "behind you" implies.

source.text: אֶת־מִ֤י חֵרַ֨פְתָּ֙ וְגִדַּ֔פְתָּ וְעַל־מִ֖י הֲרִימ֣וֹתָה קּ֑וֹל וַתִּשָּׂ֥א מָר֛וֹם עֵינֶ֖יךָ אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed, and against whom have you raised [your] voice and lifted on high your eyes? Against the Holy One of Israel.

en.L: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed, \q and against whom have you raised [your] voice \q and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!
en.B: Do you know whom you have mocked and reviled? \q At whom did you shout, \q at whom did you lift your haughty eyes? At the Holy One of Israel!
en.R: Who is it that you have insulted and spoken against? \q Who is it that you shouted at and looked at so proudly? \q It is the Holy One of Israel!

es.L: ¿A quién has afrentado y blasfemado, \q y contra quién has alzado [la] voz \q y levantado en alto tus ojos? ¡Contra el Santo de Israel!
es.B: ¿Sabes a quién has insultado y ofendido? \q ¿Contra quién gritaste, \q contra quién alzaste tus ojos altivos? ¡Contra el Santo de Israel!
es.R: ¿A quién crees que has insultado y ofendido? \q ¿A quién le gritaste y miraste con tanto orgullo? \q ¡Es al Santo de Israel!

sw.L: Ni nani uliyemtukana na kumkufuru, \q na ni juu ya nani umeinua sauti [yako] \q na kuyainua macho yako juu? Juu ya Mtakatifu wa Israeli!
sw.B: Je, unajua ni nani uliyemdhihaki na kumtukana? \q Ni nani uliyempigia kelele, \q ni nani uliyemwinulia macho yako ya kiburi? Ni Mtakatifu wa Israeli!
sw.R: Ni nani uliyemtukana na kumsema vibaya? \q Ni nani uliyempigia kelele na kumtazama kwa kiburi hivyo? \q Ni Mtakatifu wa Israeli!

decisions.choice: lifted up your eyes on high: looked with pride and contempt
decisions.reason: Lofty eyes are a picture of arrogance in Isaiah (2:11; 5:15; 10:12).

decisions.choice: the Holy One of Israel: the attack on Jerusalem was an attack on God himself
decisions.reason: Isaiah's favorite name for God comes as the answer to the questions. The king thought he was mocking a small kingdom and its god; he was defying the holy God.

source.text: בְּיַ֣ד עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ חֵרַ֣פְתָּ׀אֲדֹנָי֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרֹ֥ב רִכְבִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י עָלִ֛יתִי מְר֥וֹם הָרִ֖ים יַרְכְּתֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְאֶכְרֹ֞ת קוֹמַ֤ת אֲרָזָיו֙ מִבְחַ֣ר בְּרֹשָׁ֔יו וְאָבוֹא֙ מְר֣וֹם קִצּ֔וֹ יַ֖עַר כַּרְמִלּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: By [the] hand of your servants you have taunted [the] Lord, and you said: with [the] abundance of my chariots I have gone up [the] height of mountains, [the] far reaches of Lebanon; and I will cut down [the] tallness of its cedars, [the] choicest of its junipers; and I will come [to the] height of its end, [the] forest of its garden land.

en.L: By the hand of your servants you have taunted the Lord, \q and you said, 'With the multitude of my chariots I have gone up [to] the height of the mountains, [to] the far reaches of Lebanon, \q and I will cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest junipers, \q and I will come [to] its farthest height, the forest of its garden land.
en.B: Through your servants you have mocked the Lord. \q You said, 'With chariots past counting I have climbed the mountain heights, the far ridges of Lebanon. \q I will fell its loftiest cedars and its finest junipers. \q I will reach its farthest summit and its lush forest.
en.R: You sent your officials to insult the Lord. \q You said, 'I have many chariots. With them I have climbed the highest mountains, even the farthest mountains of Lebanon. \q I will cut down its tallest cedar trees and its best juniper trees. \q I will go to its highest peaks and its thickest forests.

es.L: Por medio de tus siervos has afrentado al Señor, \q y dijiste: ‘Con la multitud de mis carros he subido [a] la altura de los montes, [a] los lugares más remotos del Líbano, \q y cortaré sus cedros más altos, sus mejores enebros, \q y llegaré a su cumbre más lejana, al bosque de su vergel.
es.B: Por medio de tus siervos te has burlado del Señor. \q Dijiste: ‘Con carros sin número he subido a las cumbres de los montes, a las cimas lejanas del Líbano. \q Talaré sus cedros más altos y sus mejores enebros. \q Llegaré hasta su cumbre más lejana y su bosque más frondoso.
es.R: Enviaste a tus funcionarios a insultar al Señor. \q Dijiste: ‘Tengo muchos carros. Con ellos he subido a los montes más altos, hasta los montes más lejanos del Líbano. \q Cortaré sus cedros más altos y sus mejores enebros. \q Llegaré a sus cumbres más altas y a sus bosques más espesos.

sw.L: Kwa mkono wa watumishi wako umemtukana Bwana, \q ukasema, 'Kwa wingi wa magari yangu ya vita nimepanda [hata] vilele vya milima, [hata] pembe za mbali za Lebanoni, \q nami nitaikata mierezi yake mirefu, misonobari yake iliyo bora, \q nami nitafika [kwenye] kilele chake cha mbali kabisa, msitu wa bustani yake.
sw.B: Kupitia watumishi wako umemdhihaki Bwana. \q Ulisema, 'Kwa magari ya vita yasiyohesabika nimepanda vilele vya milima, matuta ya mbali ya Lebanoni. \q Nitaikata mierezi yake mirefu kuliko yote na misonobari yake iliyo bora. \q Nitafika kilele chake cha mbali kabisa na msitu wake uliositawi.
sw.R: Uliwatuma maafisa wako kumtukana Bwana. \q Ulisema, 'Nina magari mengi ya vita. Kwa magari hayo nimepanda milima mirefu kabisa, hata milima ya mbali kabisa ya Lebanoni. \q Nitaikata miti yake mirefu kabisa ya mierezi na miti yake bora ya misonobari. \q Nitakwenda kwenye vilele vyake virefu kabisa na misitu yake minene kabisa.

decisions.choice: I have gone up ... I will cut down ... I will come: boasts of what he has done and what he will do
alternatives: all past: I cut down ... I reached
decisions.reason: The first verb is a past form; the next two are forms usually read as future. The king boasts of conquests behind him and promises more. They can also be read as past ("I cut down ... I came").

decisions.choice: felling the cedars of Lebanon: a royal boast of power over the land
decisions.reason: Assyrian kings recorded in their inscriptions that they crossed mountains with their chariots and cut cedars in Lebanon for their buildings. Isaiah uses the same picture to show Assyria's pride brought down (10:33-34; 14:8).

decisions.choice: your servants ... the Lord
decisions.reason: The parallel 2 Kings 19:23 reads "your messengers". Both mean the envoys who spoke for the king (36:4-20).

decisions.choice: "watumishi wako"; "kilele chake"
decisions.reason: Isaiah has "your servants" and "its farthest height" where 2 Kings has "your messengers" and "its farthest lodging place"; the Swahili follows Isaiah in both.

source.text: אֲנִ֥י קַ֖רְתִּי וְשָׁתִ֣יתִי מָ֑יִם וְאַחְרִב֙ בְּכַף־פְּעָמַ֔י כֹּ֖ל יְאֹרֵ֥י מָצֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: I have dug and I have drunk water, and I will dry up with [the] sole of my feet all [the] streams of Egypt.

en.L: I have dug and drunk water, \q and I will dry up with the sole of my feet all the streams of Egypt.'
en.B: I have dug wells and drunk their water, \q and under the tread of my feet every stream of Egypt will run dry.'
en.R: I have dug wells and drunk water from them. \q I will march through Egypt and dry up all its streams under my feet.'

es.L: Yo he cavado y he bebido aguas, \q y secaré con la planta de mis pies todos los ríos de Egipto’.
es.B: He cavado pozos y he bebido su agua, \q y bajo la planta de mis pies se secarán todos los ríos de Egipto’.
es.R: He cavado pozos y he bebido de su agua. \q Marcharé por Egipto y secaré todos sus ríos bajo mis pies’.

sw.L: Nimechimba na kunywa maji, \q nami nitakausha kwa nyayo za miguu yangu mito yote ya Misri.'
sw.B: Nimechimba visima na kunywa maji yake, \q na chini ya nyayo za miguu yangu kila mto wa Misri utakauka.'
sw.R: Nimechimba visima na kunywa maji kutoka humo. \q Nitapita katikati ya Misri na kukausha mito yake yote chini ya miguu yangu.'

decisions.choice: Egypt: a poetic name for the land
decisions.reason: The same word is used for Egypt in 19:6. Some take it as "siege" or "fortified places".

decisions.choice: water
decisions.reason: The parallel 2 Kings 19:24 reads "foreign water", meaning he drank in lands he invaded. The sense here is the same: wherever he goes he can find water for his army.

decisions.choice: I will dry up the streams: the king claims a power that belongs to God
decisions.reason: Drying up rivers is what God does (11:15; 19:5-6; 50:2). God answers the boast in the next verse.

decisions.choice: wells
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was dug.

decisions.choice: "maji"
decisions.reason: Isaiah's Hebrew has only "water", without "foreign" as in 2 Kings; the Swahili drops "ya kigeni" accordingly.

source.text: הֲלֽוֹא־שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵאתִ֔יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לְהַשְׁא֛וֹת גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Have you not heard? From afar it I made, from days of old and I formed it; now I have brought it, and you are to lay waste [into] heaps ruined cities fortified.

en.L: Have you not heard? From long ago I did it; \q from days of old I formed it. \q Now I have brought it about, \q and you are [here] to lay waste fortified cities [into] ruined heaps.
en.B: Have you not heard? I did this long ago; \q in days of old I shaped it. \q Now I have made it happen, \q so that you turn walled cities into heaps of rubble.
en.R: Have you not heard? I planned this long ago. \q I decided it in days long past. \q Now I have made it happen. \q I let you turn strong, walled cities into piles of ruins.

es.L: ¿No has oído? Desde hace mucho lo hice; \q desde los días antiguos lo formé. \q Ahora lo he traído, \q y tú [estás] para reducir ciudades fortificadas a montones de ruinas.
es.B: ¿No lo has oído? Hace mucho tiempo que lo hice; \q en días antiguos lo planeé. \q Ahora lo he hecho realidad, \q para que tú conviertas ciudades amuralladas en montones de escombros.
es.R: ¿No lo has oído? Hace mucho tiempo que lo planeé. \q Lo decidí en días muy lejanos. \q Ahora lo he hecho realidad. \q Te permití convertir ciudades fuertes y amuralladas en montones de ruinas.

sw.L: Je, hujasikia? Tangu zamani nililifanya; \q tangu siku za kale nililiumba. \q Sasa nimelitimiza, \q nawe upo ili kuifanya miji yenye ngome kuwa magofu [na] chungu za mawe.
sw.B: Je, hujasikia? Nililifanya hili zamani; \q siku za kale nililipanga. \q Sasa nimelitimiza, \q ili wewe uigeuze miji yenye ngome kuwa chungu za kifusi.
sw.R: Je, hujasikia? Nilipanga jambo hili zamani. \q Niliamua hivyo siku nyingi zilizopita. \q Sasa nimelifanya litokee. \q Nilikuachia uigeuze miji imara yenye kuta kuwa marundo ya magofu.

decisions.choice: I made it, I formed it, I have brought it: Assyria's conquests were God's plan
decisions.reason: God answers the boast: the king did nothing on his own. God formed the plan long ago, like a potter shaping a pot (22:11), and Assyria was only his tool (10:5-15).

decisions.choice: and you are to lay waste: you exist for this purpose
decisions.reason: The verb with an infinitive describes the role God gave the king: to turn cities into ruins.

decisions.choice: I let you
decisions.reason: Readable expresses that the king's role was given to him by God.

source.text: וְיֹֽשְׁבֵיהֶן֙ קִצְרֵי־יָ֔ד חַ֖תּוּ וָבֹ֑שׁוּ הָי֞וּ עֵ֤שֶׂב שָׂדֶה֙ וִ֣ירַק דֶּ֔שֶׁא חֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֔וֹת וּשְׁדֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י קָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And their inhabitants [were] short of hand; they were dismayed and ashamed; they were plants of [the] field and green of fresh grass, grass of roofs, and a field before standing grain.

en.L: And their inhabitants [were] short of hand; \q they were dismayed and put to shame; \q they were [like] plants of the field and green herbs, \q grass of the roofs, and a field before standing grain.
en.B: Their people were powerless, \q terrified and put to shame. \q They were like the plants of the open field and fresh green herbs, \q like grass on a rooftop, like a field of young shoots before the grain stands tall.
en.R: That is why the people of those cities were weak. \q They were afraid and ashamed. \q They were like plants and grass in a field. \q They were like grass growing on a flat roof, which dries up quickly. \q They were like a field of young grain that withers before it grows tall.

es.L: Y sus habitantes [fueron] cortos de mano; \q se espantaron y fueron avergonzados; \q fueron [como] hierba del campo y verdor de hierba tierna, \q hierba de los terrados, y sembrado antes de [ser] mies en pie.
es.B: Sus habitantes quedaron sin fuerzas, \q aterrados y avergonzados. \q Fueron como las plantas del campo y la hierba verde y tierna, \q como la hierba de los terrados, como un sembrado de brotes antes de que la mies se alce.
es.R: Por eso la gente de esas ciudades estaba débil. \q Tenían miedo y vergüenza. \q Eran como plantas y hierba en el campo. \q Eran como la hierba que crece sobre un techo plano, que se seca enseguida. \q Eran como un campo de trigo tierno que se marchita antes de crecer.

sw.L: Na wakazi wake [walikuwa] wafupi wa mkono; \q walifadhaika na kuaibika; \q walikuwa [kama] mimea ya shambani na majani mabichi, \q majani ya juu ya dari, na shamba kabla ya ngano kusimama.
sw.B: Watu wake walikosa nguvu, \q wakaogopa na kuaibika. \q Walikuwa kama mimea ya mashambani na majani mabichi, \q kama nyasi juu ya paa, kama shamba la machipukizi kabla nafaka haijakua mirefu.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu watu wa miji hiyo walikuwa dhaifu. \q Waliogopa na kuona aibu. \q Walikuwa kama mimea na nyasi shambani. \q Walikuwa kama nyasi zinazoota juu ya paa la nyumba, zinazokauka upesi. \q Walikuwa kama shamba la nafaka changa inayonyauka kabla haijakua mirefu.

decisions.choice: short of hand: without power
decisions.reason: A short hand cannot reach or act (50:2; 59:1). The cities' people had no strength to resist.

decisions.choice: a field before standing grain: young shoots that have not grown up and wither easily
alternatives: scorched before it is grown (2 Kings 19:26)
decisions.reason: The phrase is difficult. The parallel 2 Kings 19:26 reads "scorched before it is grown", and the Great Isaiah Scroll appears to read "scorched before the east wind". All the readings picture young growth that is easily destroyed.

decisions.choice: grass of the roofs: grass sprouting in the thin soil of flat roofs
decisions.reason: Such grass withers before it grows (Psalm 129:6).

decisions.choice: That is why; which dries up quickly; that withers
decisions.reason: Readable states the link with verse 26 and the point of the comparisons.

decisions.choice: "shamba kabla ya ngano kusimama"
decisions.reason: Isaiah reads "a field before standing grain" where 2 Kings has "scorched before it is standing grain"; the Swahili follows Isaiah.

source.text: וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ וְצֵאתְךָ֥ וּבוֹאֲךָ֖ יָדָ֑עְתִּי וְאֵ֖ת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ֥ אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And your sitting down and your going out and your coming in I know, and your raging against me.

en.L: And your sitting down and your going out and your coming in I know, \q and your raging against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: I know where you sit, when you go out and when you come in, \q and how you storm against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I know everything you do. I know when you rest and when you come and go. \q And I know how angry you are with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y tu sentarte, y tu salir y tu entrar yo conozco, \q y tu furor contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Yo sé dónde te sientas, cuándo sales y cuándo entras, \q y cómo te enfureces contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Yo sé todo lo que haces. Sé cuándo descansas y cuándo vas y vienes. \q Y sé cuánto te enfureces contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

sw.L: Na kuketi kwako na kutoka kwako na kuingia kwako ninajua, \q na ghadhabu yako juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Ninajua uketipo, utokapo na uingiapo, \q na jinsi unavyonighadhibikia.
sw.R: Ninajua kila kitu unachofanya. Ninajua unapopumzika na unapotoka na kuingia. \q Na ninajua jinsi ulivyo na hasira dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

decisions.choice: your sitting, your going out, your coming in: everything you do
decisions.reason: The pairs sum up all of a person's life and actions (Deuteronomy 28:6; Psalm 121:8; 139:2). Nothing the king does is hidden from God.

decisions.choice: raging: a stirred-up, violent anger
decisions.reason: The verb means to tremble or be agitated, here with fury against God.

decisions.choice: I know everything you do
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense of the pairs first.

source.text: יַ֚עַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ֣ אֵלַ֔י וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ֖ עָלָ֣ה בְאָזְנָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁ֣יבֹתִ֔יךָ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אתָ בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Because your raging against me and your arrogance has come up into my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.

en.L: Because of your raging against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and your arrogance has come up into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears, \q I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hook in your nose and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bridle in your lips, \q and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.
en.B: Since you rage against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and your arrogance has come up to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears, \q I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hook in your nose and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bit between your lips, \q and I will lead you back along the same road by which you came.
en.R: You have been angry with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and I have heard your proud words. \q So I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hook through your nose and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bit between your lips, as people do to lead an animal. \q I will force you to go back home by the same road you came on.

es.L: Por tu furor contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q y [porque] tu arrogancia ha subido a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} oídos, \q pondré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} garfio en tu nariz y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} freno en tus labios, \q y te haré volver por el camino por donde viniste.
es.B: Ya que te enfureces contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} \q y tu arrogancia ha llegado a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} oídos, \q te pondré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} garfio en la nariz y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} freno entre los labios, \q y te haré volver por el mismo camino por el que viniste.
es.R: Te has enfurecido contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q y he oído tus palabras orgullosas. \q Por eso te pondré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} garfio en la nariz y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} freno entre los labios, como se hace para llevar a un animal. \q Te obligaré a volver a tu tierra por el mismo camino por el que viniste.

sw.L: Kwa sababu ya ghadhabu yako juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q na kiburi chako kimepanda masikioni {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}, \q nitatia ndoana {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} puani mwako na lijamu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} midomoni mwako, \q nami nitakurudisha kwa njia ile uliyoijia.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa unanighadhibikia \q na kiburi chako kimefika masikioni {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}, \q nitatia ndoana {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} puani mwako na hatamu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kati ya midomo yako, \q nami nitakurudisha kwa njia ile ile uliyoijia.
sw.R: Umenikasirikia, \q nami nimesikia maneno yako ya kiburi. \q Kwa hiyo nitatia ndoana {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} puani mwako na hatamu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kati ya midomo yako, kama watu wanavyomwongoza mnyama. \q Nitakulazimisha urudi kwenu kwa njia ile ile uliyoijia.

decisions.choice: a hook in the nose, a bridle in the lips: led away like a beast or a captive
decisions.reason: Animals were led by rings through the nose (Ezekiel 19:4; 29:4), and Assyrian kings showed captive rulers led by cords fastened to their lips. God will treat the conqueror as he treated others.

decisions.choice: your arrogance: proud, careless confidence
decisions.reason: The word describes a person at ease who thinks nothing can touch him (32:9).

decisions.choice: turn you back by the way you came: fulfilled when he goes home
decisions.reason: The promise is repeated in verse 34 and fulfilled in verse 37.

decisions.choice: as people do to lead an animal; back home
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture and where the road leads (verse 37).

source.text: וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת אָכ֤וֹל הַשָּׁנָה֙ סָפִ֔יחַ וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית שָׁחִ֑יס וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗ית זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים וְאִכְל֥וּ פִרְיָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] for you the sign: eating this year aftergrowth, and in the year the second self-sown grain, and in the year the third sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

en.L: And this [is] the sign for you: \q eating this year what grows by itself, \q and in the second year what springs up from that, \q and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
en.B: Here is the sign for you: \q this year you will live on grain that sprang up untended, \q and next year on whatever comes up after it; \q but in the third year, sow and harvest, plant vineyards and eat what they bear.
en.R: Hezekiah, this will be a sign for you. \q This year you will eat grain that grows wild. \q Next year you will eat grain that comes up from that. \q But in the third year you will plant your crops and harvest them. You will plant vineyards and eat their grapes.

es.L: Y esta [será] la señal para ti: \q comer este año lo que nace por sí mismo, \q y el segundo año lo que brota de ello, \q y el tercer año {{plural_you:siembren|sembrad}} y {{plural_you:sieguen|segad}}, y {{plural_you:planten|plantad}} viñas y {{plural_you:coman|comed}} su fruto.
es.B: Esta es la señal para ti: \q este año {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} del grano que brotó sin sembrarlo, \q y el año próximo de lo que salga después; \q pero el tercer año {{plural_you:siembren|sembrad}} y {{plural_you:cosechen|cosechad}}, {{plural_you:planten|plantad}} viñas y {{plural_you:coman|comed}} de su fruto.
es.R: Ezequías, esta será una señal para ti: \q Este año {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} el grano que crece solo. \q El año próximo {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} el grano que brote de ese. \q Pero el tercer año {{plural_you:sembrarán|sembraréis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cultivos y los {{plural_you:cosecharán|cosecharéis}}. {{plural_you:Plantarán|Plantaréis}} viñas y {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} sus uvas.

sw.L: Na hii [ndiyo] ishara kwako: \q mwaka huu mtakula kinachoota chenyewe, \q na mwaka wa pili kinachochipuka katika hicho, \q na mwaka wa tatu pandeni na kuvuna, mpande mashamba ya mizabibu na kula matunda yake.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo ishara kwako: \q mwaka huu mtaishi kwa nafaka iliyoota yenyewe, \q na mwaka ujao kwa chochote kitakachoota kutoka kwake; \q lakini mwaka wa tatu pandeni na kuvuna, pandeni mashamba ya mizabibu na mle matunda yake.
sw.R: Hezekia, hii itakuwa ishara kwako. \q Mwaka huu mtakula nafaka inayoota yenyewe porini. \q Mwaka ujao mtakula nafaka itakayochipuka kutoka kwa hiyo. \q Lakini mwaka wa tatu mtapanda mazao yenu na kuyavuna. Mtapanda mashamba ya mizabibu na kula zabibu zake.

decisions.choice: what grows by itself: grain sprouting from seed spilled at the last harvest
decisions.reason: With the Assyrian army in the land, no crops could be sown. The words are those used for the sabbatical year (Leviticus 25:5, 11). The people will live on what comes up without sowing until normal farming returns.

decisions.choice: the sign for you: addressed to Hezekiah, with commands to the people
decisions.reason: "You" is singular, but "sow", "reap" and "plant" are plural. The sign is confirmed after the event, as in Exodus 3:12: the people will live to farm in peace again.

decisions.choice: and eat: the reading of the traditional reading notes
decisions.reason: The written text has the infinitive "and eating"; the margin reads the plural command "and eat". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed; Isaiah turns from Sennacherib to the king.

source.text: וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית־יְהוּדָ֛ה הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ לְמָ֑טָּה וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י לְמָֽעְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will add the escaped of the house of Judah that remains [to take] root downward and will produce fruit upward.

en.L: And the escaped of the house of Judah that remains will again [take] root downward \q and bear fruit upward.
en.B: Those of the house of Judah who escape and are left will once more put down roots below \q and bear fruit above.
en.R: Once again the people of Judah who are left will be like a plant. \q They will send their roots down deep and grow fruit up high.

es.L: Y lo que haya escapado de la casa de Judá, lo que quede, volverá a echar raíces abajo \q y dará fruto arriba.
es.B: Los de la casa de Judá que escapen y queden volverán a echar raíces abajo \q y a dar fruto arriba.
es.R: Otra vez la gente de Judá que quede será como una planta. \q Echará raíces profundas y dará fruto en lo alto.

sw.L: Na waliookoka wa nyumba ya Yuda waliobaki wataongeza [kutia] mizizi chini \q na kuzaa matunda juu.
sw.B: Wale wa nyumba ya Yuda watakaookoka na kubaki watatia tena mizizi chini \q na kuzaa matunda juu.
sw.R: Kwa mara nyingine tena watu wa Yuda waliobaki watakuwa kama mmea. \q Watatia mizizi yao chini sana na kuzaa matunda juu.

decisions.choice: the escaped that remains: the survivors of Judah
decisions.reason: The same words describe those who survive God's judgment in 4:2 and 10:20.

decisions.choice: root below and fruit above: new life and prosperity
decisions.reason: A plant rooted deep and bearing fruit is a picture of a people restored (27:6; compare the reverse in Amos 2:9).

decisions.choice: will be like a plant
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison explicit.

source.text: כִּ֤י מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ תֵּצֵ֣א שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה מֵהַ֣ר צִיּ֑וֹן קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־זֹּֽאת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For from Jerusalem will go out a remnant, and an escaped [band] from [the] mountain of Zion. The zeal of Yahweh of hosts will do this.

en.L: For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, \q and an escaped band from Mount Zion. \q The zeal of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will do this.
en.B: For a remnant will go out from Jerusalem, \q and from Mount Zion those who have escaped. \q The burning zeal of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will make this happen.
en.R: A group of survivors will come out of Jerusalem, \q out of Mount Zion. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart on doing this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do it.

es.L: Porque de Jerusalén saldrá un remanente, \q y del monte Sion los que escapen. \q El celo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los ejércitos hará esto.
es.B: Porque de Jerusalén saldrá un remanente, \q y del monte Sion, los que hayan escapado. \q El ardiente celo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos hará que esto suceda.
es.R: Un grupo de sobrevivientes saldrá de Jerusalén, \q del monte Sion. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos ha puesto {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} corazón en hacerlo, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} lo hará.

sw.L: Kwa maana kutoka Yerusalemu mabaki watatoka, \q na kundi lililookoka kutoka mlima Sayuni. \q Wivu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi utafanya hili.
sw.B: Kwa maana mabaki watatoka Yerusalemu, \q na walionusurika kutoka mlima Sayuni. \q Wivu mkali wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi utalitimiza jambo hili.
sw.R: Kundi la watu walionusurika litatoka Yerusalemu, \q kutoka mlima Sayuni. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ameweka moyo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} juu ya kufanya jambo hili, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atalifanya.

decisions.choice: will go out: the survivors leave the city freely once the siege is over
decisions.reason: The people shut up in Jerusalem will go out again to live and farm (verses 30-31).

decisions.choice: the zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this: the same words as 9:6
decisions.reason: God's burning commitment to his people guarantees the promise. In the parallel 2 Kings 19:31 the written text lacks "of hosts", which the margin supplies.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לֹ֤א יָבוֹא֙ אֶל־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹֽא־יוֹרֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם חֵ֑ץ וְלֹֽא־יְקַדְּמֶ֣נָּה מָגֵ֔ן וְלֹֽא־יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ עֳלֶ֖יהָסֹלְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh concerning [the] king of Assyria: not he will come into the city this, and not he will shoot there an arrow, and not he will come before it [with a] shield, and not he will pour out against it a siege mound.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning the king of Assyria: \q He will not come into this city, \q and he will not shoot an arrow there, \q and he will not come before it [with] a shield, \q and he will not pour out a siege mound against it.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this about the king of Assyria: \q He will never set foot in this city. \q He will not fire a single arrow into it, \q nor face it with a shield, \q nor pile up an earthen ramp against its walls.
en.R: So, about the king of Assyria, this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q He will not come into this city. \q He will not shoot even one arrow here. \q His soldiers will not march up to it with shields. \q They will not build a ramp of dirt against its walls.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca del rey de Asiria: \q No entrará en esta ciudad, \q ni lanzará allí flecha, \q ni vendrá delante de ella [con] escudo, \q ni levantará contra ella terraplén.
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto acerca del rey de Asiria: \q Jamás pondrá un pie en esta ciudad. \q No disparará contra ella ni una flecha, \q ni se le enfrentará con escudo, \q ni levantará una rampa de tierra contra sus muros.
es.R: Por eso, acerca del rey de Asiria, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q No entrará en esta ciudad. \q No disparará aquí ni una sola flecha. \q Sus soldados no se acercarán a ella con escudos. \q No construirán una rampa de tierra contra sus muros.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo asemavyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kuhusu mfalme wa Ashuru: \q Hataingia katika mji huu, \q wala hatapiga mshale humo, \q wala hatakuja mbele yake [na] ngao, \q wala hatamwaga boma juu yake.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo kuhusu mfalme wa Ashuru: \q Hatakanyaga kamwe katika mji huu. \q Hatapiga hata mshale mmoja ndani yake, \q wala hataukabili kwa ngao, \q wala hatajenga boma la udongo dhidi ya kuta zake.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, kuhusu mfalme wa Ashuru, hiki ndicho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anachosema: \q Hataingia katika mji huu. \q Hatapiga hata mshale mmoja hapa. \q Askari wake hawataukaribia wakiwa na ngao. \q Hawatajenga boma la udongo dhidi ya kuta zake.

decisions.choice: pour out a siege mound: heap up an earthen ramp against the wall
decisions.reason: Attackers built ramps of earth and stone to bring battering rams up to a city's walls. The Assyrian siege ramp at Lachish has been excavated.

decisions.choice: he will not come into this city: a promise of complete protection
decisions.reason: Not only will the city not fall; the siege will not even begin. Sennacherib's own annals say he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem, but they do not claim that he took the city.

decisions.choice: His soldiers ... They
decisions.reason: Readable names the army that would carry the shields and build the ramp; the king acts through it.

source.text: בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖א בָּ֣הּ יָשׁ֑וּב וְאֶל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: By the way that he came, by it he will return, and into the city this not he will come, declares Yahweh.

en.L: By the way by which he came, by it he will return, \q and into this city he will not come, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The road that brought him here will take him back again. \q This city he will not enter, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He will go back home the same way he came. \q He will not come into this city, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Por el camino por donde vino, por él volverá, \q y en esta ciudad no entrará, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: El camino que lo trajo aquí lo llevará de vuelta. \q En esta ciudad no entrará, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Regresará a su tierra por el mismo camino por el que vino. \q No entrará en esta ciudad, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Kwa njia aliyoijia, kwa njia hiyo atarudi, \q wala hataingia katika mji huu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Njia iliyomleta hapa ndiyo itakayomrudisha. \q Mji huu hataingia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Atarudi kwao kwa njia ile ile aliyoijia. \q Hataingia katika mji huu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: by the way he came he will return: repeats verse 29
decisions.reason: The promise to the king of Assyria matches the end of the poem (verse 29) and comes true in verse 37.

decisions.choice: dice el SEÑOR
decisions.reason: As the terms note asks, the Literal keeps "dice" from 2 Kings 19:33, where the Hebrew is the same, instead of the block's usual "declara".

source.text: וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will defend over the city this to save it, for my sake and for the sake of David my servant.

en.L: And I will defend this city, to save it, \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake and for the sake of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant."
en.B: I will shield this city and rescue it, \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own sake and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David's sake."
en.R: I will protect this city and save it. \q I will do this for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own honor, and because of the promise I made to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David."

es.L: Y yo ampararé esta ciudad para salvarla, \q por amor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo y por amor de David {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo».
es.B: Yo protegeré esta ciudad y la salvaré, \q por amor a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo y por amor a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David».
es.R: Yo protegeré esta ciudad y la salvaré. \q Lo haré por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propia honra, y por la promesa que le hice a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David».

sw.L: Nami nitaulinda mji huu, ili kuuokoa, \q kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili ya Daudi mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.B: Nitaukinga mji huu na kuuokoa, \q kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mwenyewe na kwa ajili ya mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Daudi."
sw.R: Nitaulinda mji huu na kuuokoa. \q Nitafanya hivyo kwa ajili ya heshima {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mwenyewe, na kwa sababu ya ahadi niliyompa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Daudi."

decisions.choice: defend: cover over and shield
decisions.reason: The verb pictures God spreading his protection over the city (31:5; 38:6).

decisions.choice: for my sake and for David's sake: God acts for his own name and his promise to David
decisions.reason: God saves to uphold his honor before the nations (verse 20; 43:25; 48:11) and to keep his promise that David's line would rule in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 7:16; 1 Kings 11:13).

decisions.choice: for my own honor; because of the promise I made to my servant David
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "for my sake" and "for David's sake" mean.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א׀מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּכֶּה֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה אַשּׁ֔וּר מֵאָ֛ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֥ה כֻלָּ֖ם פְּגָרִ֥ים מֵתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] angel of Yahweh and struck down in [the] camp of Assyria a hundred and eighty-five thousand; and they rose early in the morning, and look, all of them [were] corpses, dead.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went out and struck down in the camp of Assyria 185,000; and they rose early in the morning, and look, all of them [were] dead bodies.
en.B: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} then went out and struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. At dawn, when people got up, they found them all lying dead.
en.R: Then the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went out to the camp of the Assyrian army and killed 185,000 soldiers. Early the next morning, when people woke up, they saw that all of those soldiers were dead.

es.L: Y el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} salió e hirió en el campamento de Asiria a 185 000; y cuando se levantaron de madrugada, he aquí que todos ellos [eran] cadáveres.
es.B: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} salió al campamento asirio e hirió de muerte a 185 000. Al amanecer, cuando la gente se levantó, los encontraron a todos muertos.
es.R: Entonces el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} fue al campamento del ejército asirio y mató a 185 000 soldados. A la mañana siguiente, cuando la gente se levantó, vio que todos esos soldados estaban muertos.

sw.L: Naye malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akatoka, akapiga katika kambi ya Ashuru 185,000; nao walipoamka asubuhi na mapema, tazama, wote [walikuwa] maiti.
sw.B: Kisha malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alitoka, akaenda katika kambi ya Waashuru, akawaua watu 185,000. Watu walipoamka alfajiri, wakawakuta wote wamelala wamekufa.
sw.R: Kisha malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikwenda katika kambi ya jeshi la Ashuru, akawaua askari 185,000. Asubuhi na mapema watu walipoamka, waliona kwamba askari wale wote walikuwa wamekufa.

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD: God's messenger acting with his power
decisions.reason: The angel of the LORD carries out God's judgment, as on Egypt's firstborn (Exodus 12:23) and on Israel in David's time (2 Samuel 24:16). The text does not say how the soldiers died.

decisions.choice: they rose early: people, not named
decisions.reason: The subject is not the dead soldiers but those who rose in the morning, whether survivors in the camp or people of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the end of the campaign: Assyria's records do not report the capture of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Sennacherib's annals boast that he shut Hezekiah in Jerusalem "like a bird in a cage" and received heavy tribute, but tell of no capture. The Greek historian Herodotus (Histories 2.141) records an Egyptian story of a disaster that struck Sennacherib's army in one night.

decisions.choice: men (B); soldiers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the 185,000 were.

Numbers of four or more digits are written in figures with a space in Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezra, as the English writes 185,000; 2 Kings 19:35 as published spells the number out, and this is the only change from it in the verse.

decisions.choice: no "usiku ule"
decisions.reason: Isaiah lacks "that night", which opens the verse in 2 Kings; the Swahili leaves it out.

source.text: וַיִּסַּ֣ע וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖שָׁב סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּנִֽינְוֵֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out and went and returned Sennacherib king of Assyria, and he stayed in Nineveh.

en.L: And Sennacherib king of Assyria set out and went and returned, and he stayed in Nineveh.
en.B: So Sennacherib king of Assyria struck camp and went away. He returned home and stayed in Nineveh.
en.R: So King Sennacherib of Assyria packed up his camp and left. He went back to Nineveh, his capital city, and lived there.

es.L: Y Senaquerib, rey de Asiria, partió, y se fue y regresó, y se quedó en Nínive.
es.B: Así que Senaquerib, rey de Asiria, levantó el campamento y se fue. Regresó a su tierra y se quedó en Nínive.
es.R: Así que el rey Senaquerib de Asiria levantó su campamento y se fue. Regresó a Nínive, su capital, y vivió allí.

sw.L: Naye Senakeribu mfalme wa Ashuru akaondoka, akaenda, akarudi, akakaa Ninawi.
sw.B: Basi Senakeribu mfalme wa Ashuru aliivunja kambi yake, akaondoka. Akarudi kwao, akakaa Ninawi.
sw.R: Basi mfalme Senakeribu wa Ashuru alikusanya kambi yake, akaondoka. Akarudi Ninawi, mji wake mkuu, akaishi huko.

decisions.choice: Nineveh: the capital of Assyria under Sennacherib
decisions.reason: Sennacherib rebuilt Nineveh, on the Tigris River, as his royal city.

decisions.choice: returned: God's word comes true
decisions.reason: The king goes home as God said he would (verses 7, 29, 34).

decisions.choice: his capital city
decisions.reason: Readable explains what Nineveh was.

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית׀נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר בָּנָיו֙ הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, he [was] bowing down [in the] house of Nisroch his god, and Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword, and they escaped [to the] land of Ararat. And became king Esarhaddon his son in his place.

en.L: And it was, [as] he [was] bowing down [in] the house of Nisroch his god, [that] Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword, and they escaped [to] the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.
en.B: While he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his own sons, cut him down with the sword and fled to the land of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.
en.R: Later, Sennacherib was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch. While he was there, two of his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with a sword. Then they ran away to the land of Ararat, in the mountains to the north. Another son, Esarhaddon, became the next king of Assyria.

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras él se postraba [en] la casa de Nisroc su dios, Adramelec y Sarezer, sus hijos, lo hirieron a espada, y huyeron [a] la tierra de Ararat. Y reinó en su lugar Esarhadón su hijo.
es.B: Mientras adoraba postrado en el templo de Nisroc, su dios, sus propios hijos Adramelec y Sarezer lo mataron a espada y huyeron a la tierra de Ararat. Su hijo Esarhadón reinó en su lugar.
es.R: Tiempo después, Senaquerib estaba adorando en el templo de su dios Nisroc. Mientras estaba allí, dos de sus hijos, Adramelec y Sarezer, lo mataron con una espada. Después huyeron a la tierra de Ararat, en las montañas del norte. Otro de sus hijos, Esarhadón, llegó a ser el nuevo rey de Asiria.

sw.L: Ikawa, alipokuwa akisujudu [katika] nyumba ya Nisroki mungu wake, Adrameleki na Shareza wanawe wakampiga kwa upanga, nao wakakimbilia [katika] nchi ya Ararati. Na Esar-hadoni mwanawe akawa mfalme mahali pake.
sw.B: Alipokuwa akisujudu katika nyumba ya Nisroki mungu wake, Adrameleki na Shareza, wanawe mwenyewe, walimuua kwa upanga, wakakimbilia nchi ya Ararati. Na mwanawe Esar-hadoni akatawala mahali pake.
sw.R: Baadaye Senakeribu alikuwa akiabudu katika hekalu la mungu wake Nisroki. Alipokuwa huko, wanawe wawili, Adrameleki na Shareza, walimuua kwa upanga. Kisha wakakimbilia nchi ya Ararati, katika milima ya upande wa kaskazini. Mwanawe mwingine, Esar-hadoni, akawa mfalme wa Ashuru baada yake.

decisions.choice: his death: Sennacherib was murdered in 681 BC, about twenty years after the campaign
decisions.reason: The Babylonian Chronicle records that Sennacherib was killed by his son in a revolt, and that Esarhaddon followed him as king. This fulfills the word of verse 7: he fell by the sword in his own land.

decisions.choice: Nisroch: an Assyrian god not otherwise known by this name
decisions.reason: The god's identity is uncertain; the name may be a form of the name of a known Assyrian god.

decisions.choice: the land of Ararat: Urartu, a kingdom in the mountains north of Assyria
decisions.reason: The same name is used for the mountains where the ark came to rest (Genesis 8:4). Urartu was Assyria's rival, a refuge beyond its reach.

decisions.choice: Later; in the mountains to the north
decisions.reason: Readable marks that the murder came years after the campaign (see m1) and locates Ararat.
